title: Supreme Court warns States that FIR must be registered immediately for every missing person
summary: The Supreme Court stressed the need for immediate registration of FIRs in missing-person cases irrespective of the age or gender of the missing person, emphasising prompt police action.

title: Supreme Court seeks ECI data on appeals decided by West Bengal SIR appellate tribunals
summary: The Supreme Court sought data from the Election Commission of India regarding the number of appeals disposed of by appellate tribunals in proceedings connected with the West Bengal Special Intensive Revision.

title: Supreme Court seeks Union response on mechanism to block illegal AI-generated and doxxed content
summary: The Supreme Court directed the Union Government to consider a representation seeking an urgent mechanism for reporting and blocking unlawful AI-generated or doxxing-related online content.

title: Supreme Court asks Centre and BCI to respond on commercial exploitation of courtroom observations
summary: The Supreme Court sought responses from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the Bar Council of India concerning alleged commercial exploitation and monetisation of oral courtroom observations.

title: Supreme Court seeks Centre response on plea concerning fake advocates
summary: The Supreme Court sought a response from the Union Government on a plea concerning alleged fake advocates and the unauthorised commercial exploitation of courtroom proceedings and observations.

title: Supreme Court restores acquittal in minor rape case after finding forensic evidence insufficient
summary: In Ram Singh v. State of Himachal Pradesh, the Supreme Court restored the trial court's acquittal after finding that the High Court had not properly considered medical and forensic evidence.

title: Supreme Court explains when alibi can be considered before trial in criminal cases
summary: The Supreme Court held that there is no inflexible rule that an accused can establish an alibi only during trial and explained circumstances in which defence material may justify quashing proceedings at the pre-trial stage.

title: Supreme Court explains principles governing judicial review of examination evaluation
summary: The Supreme Court considered the limits of judicial review in disputes involving examination evaluation and explained when courts may interfere with academic assessment.

title: Supreme Court explains parameters for admitting additional evidence under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC
summary: The Supreme Court examined the requirements governing applications for additional evidence at the appellate stage under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

title: Supreme Court grants compensation to Shaurya Chakra awardee's widow
summary: The Supreme Court granted compensation of ₹10 lakh to the widow of a Shaurya Chakra awardee while dealing with the relevant legal and factual circumstances.

title: Supreme Court considers West Bengal SIR appellate tribunal disposal timelines
summary: The Supreme Court examined the functioning of appellate tribunals dealing with objections arising from the electoral-roll revision process and sought information concerning disposal of appeals.

title: Delhi High Court orders status quo in long-running Ambassador Hotel property dispute
summary: The Delhi High Court stayed the operation of an appellate court decree and directed parties to maintain status quo concerning the Ambassador Hotel property dispute involving the Central Government and private owners.

title: Delhi High Court denies bail to Olympian wrestler Sushil Kumar
summary: The Delhi High Court denied bail to Olympic medallist Sushil Kumar in the Sagar Dhankar murder case arising from the 2021 incident at Chhatrasal Stadium.

title: Delhi High Court asks Centre to consider removal of inflammatory online content concerning Shirdi Sai Baba
summary: The Delhi High Court directed the Centre to consider representations seeking removal of allegedly inflammatory and derogatory online content concerning Shri Sai Baba.

title: Delhi High Court to examine whether social-media accounts can be suspended for copyright strikes
summary: The Delhi High Court framed a preliminary issue concerning whether social-media platforms can suspend or delete accounts based on copyright strikes and directed major platforms to respond.

title: Delhi High Court directs takedown of obscene content concerning actress Janhvi Kapoor
summary: The Delhi High Court considered personality-rights concerns and directed action concerning obscene online content while questioning the scope of blanket restrictions on fan pages.

title: Delhi High Court refuses to interfere with NEET-UG 2026 final answer key
summary: The Delhi High Court declined to interfere with the NTA's final answer key, observing that courts should not substitute their assessment for that of subject experts unless an answer is demonstrably incorrect.

title: Delhi High Court examines taxability of judicial allowances and seeks PAN details
summary: The Delhi High Court directed relevant authorities concerning Supreme Court and High Court judges to provide PAN-related details amid a dispute concerning taxability of judicial allowances.

title: Madras High Court questions denial of permit for anti-NEET and EWS bike rally
summary: The Madras High Court questioned restrictions imposed on a proposed bike rally and emphasised that the State cannot suppress citizens' lawful expression and assembly.

title: Madras High Court holds disability reservation cannot be claimed for engagement as government lawyer
summary: The Madras High Court considered the applicability of disability reservation in appointments or engagements as government lawyers and ruled on the claim before it.

title: Madras High Court defers framing of charge in cash-for-vote case
summary: The Madras High Court deferred framing of charges in a cash-for-vote case involving BJP leader Nainar Nagendran and others.

title: Bombay High Court extends attendance protection to law students across semesters
summary: The Bombay High Court held that the Supreme Court's one-time protection concerning detention for attendance shortage applies to law students across semesters and not merely final-year students.

title: Bombay High Court allows ILS Law College students with attendance shortage to sit examinations
summary: The Bombay High Court permitted students of ILS Law College affected by attendance shortage to appear for semester examinations and extended the benefit to similarly situated students.

title: Bombay High Court considers law-college seat cuts linked to faculty approval timelines
summary: The Bombay High Court examined disputes involving reductions in law-college student intake and university action concerning approval of teaching staff and principals.

title: Allahabad High Court orders inquiry after police allegedly failed to register FIR in digital rape case
summary: The Allahabad High Court ordered an inquiry against senior police officers after allegations that an FIR was not registered despite a complaint involving digital rape, molestation and related offences.

title: Allahabad High Court says police cannot refuse FIR merely because complainant has not produced evidence
summary: The Allahabad High Court emphasised that police cannot refuse registration of an FIR in a sexual-harassment complaint merely because the complainant has not initially produced evidence.

title: Gujarat High Court rules private playing cards without profit-making element do not constitute gambling offence
summary: The Gujarat High Court examined a case involving playing cards for money and held that the absence of a profit-making element can be relevant to determining whether the activity constitutes an offence under gambling law.

title: Calcutta High Court permits Jamiat rally concerning removal of loudspeakers from mosques
summary: The Calcutta High Court permitted a rally concerning removal of loudspeakers from mosques while imposing a cap of 750 participants.

title: Punjab and Haryana High Court applies PMLA Section 45 bail exception to women without distinction
summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court considered the special bail exception under Section 45 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and held that it applies to women without distinction based on education, status or profession.

title: Karnataka High Court permits chargesheet in disappearance of 21 stray dogs from DRDO township
summary: The Karnataka High Court permitted police to file a chargesheet after investigation into the disappearance of 21 stray dogs from a DRDO township in Bengaluru.

title: Rajasthan High Court flags forged birth certificates being used in habeas corpus cases
summary: The Rajasthan High Court raised concerns over forged or illegally issued birth certificates allegedly being used to portray missing minor girls as adults and directed authorities to strengthen verification.

title: Delhi High Court examines PMLA proceedings after predicate offence is quashed on compromise
summary: The Delhi High Court considered whether proceedings under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act automatically disappear merely because the underlying predicate offence was quashed on the basis of compromise.

title: Allahabad High Court directs action concerning police refusal to register sexual-harassment FIR
summary: The Allahabad High Court directed an inquiry by senior police authorities after allegations that a woman's sexual-harassment complaint against her employer was not registered as an FIR.

title: Supreme Court daily roundup records major constitutional and criminal-law developments
summary: The Supreme Court's August 11 daily developments included proceedings concerning missing persons, electoral-roll appeals, criminal law, compensation and online content regulation.

title: Supreme Court adjourns challenge to Sambhal mosque survey order to August 18
summary: The Supreme Court has adjourned until August 18 the hearing on petitions challenging the judicial order directing a survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid at Sambhal, keeping the constitutional and procedural issues before the Court alive.

title: Supreme Court declines to interfere with Calcutta High Court orders on frozen TMC bank accounts
summary: The Supreme Court has declined to interfere with Calcutta High Court directions governing the operation of three bank accounts of the Trinamool Congress, leaving the High Court's restrictions in place.

title: Parliament passes Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026
summary: Parliament has passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026. The legislation proposes changes to the institutional framework governing national tribunals and is aimed at restructuring the administration of tribunal functions.

title: BCI asks State Bar Councils to prepare panel of women members for co-option
summary: The Bar Council of India has asked State Bar Councils to meet on August 16 to prepare a panel of four women members for co-option, with the proposed panels to be forwarded to the Chief Justices of the respective High Courts.

title: Justice Vikram Nath stresses accountability of institutions exercising public power
summary: Supreme Court Justice Vikram Nath has emphasised that institutions must remain open to questioning and accountable for the exercise of public power, highlighting the importance of constitutional accountability.

title: Gujarat High Court considers legality of playing cards for money at home
summary: The Gujarat High Court has considered the legal position concerning playing cards for money in a private setting and whether the absence of a profit-making element attracts liability under the applicable gambling law.

title: Delhi High Court reiterates importance of respecting women's autonomy and dignity
summary: The Delhi High Court has addressed questions concerning women's clothing and sexual harassment, emphasising that responsibility for inappropriate conduct cannot be shifted onto women through policing of their clothing or appearance.

title: High Courts issue fresh legal developments across India
summary: A compilation of developments from India's High Courts on August 11 covers criminal law, constitutional issues, procedural questions and other significant judicial decisions from different jurisdictions.

title: LiveLaw launches breaking legal news alerts
summary: LiveLaw has introduced a breaking-news alert feature aimed at delivering important developments from India's courts and legal system more rapidly to readers.

title: Indian courts continue to expand protection of women's autonomy
summary: Recent judicial developments have addressed women's autonomy, choice of partner, workplace rights and protection from gender-based stereotyping, forming part of a wider constitutional jurisprudence on dignity and equality.

title: Weekly legal developments highlight major Supreme Court and High Court decisions
summary: A review of legal developments from August 3 to 9 covers important decisions involving criminal law, constitutional questions, gender rights, live-in relationships and other areas of Indian law.

title: President assents to law increasing sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges to 38
summary: President Droupadi Murmu has given assent to the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026, increasing the sanctioned strength of judges of the Supreme Court. The measure is intended to strengthen the Court's capacity to deal with its substantial judicial workload.

title: Supreme Court moots dedicated afternoon slot for long-pending Constitution Bench matters
summary: The Supreme Court has considered creating a dedicated afternoon hearing slot for long-pending Constitution Bench matters. The proposal seeks to ensure that important constitutional cases receive focused hearing time and progress towards final adjudication.

title: Supreme Court defers Cauvery dispute hearing to August 17
summary: The Supreme Court has deferred the hearing on Tamil Nadu's plea concerning directions to Karnataka in relation to the Cauvery water dispute. The matter has been listed for further consideration on August 17, 2026.

title: Supreme Court refuses uniform policy on demolition of long-standing unauthorised properties
summary: The Supreme Court declined to entertain a plea seeking a nationwide uniform policy governing regularisation and demolition of long-standing unauthorised constructions. The Court indicated that the formulation of such broad policy primarily falls within the policy domain.

title: Supreme Court overturns anticipatory bail relief granted by Bombay High Court in premature plea
summary: The Supreme Court held that a High Court cannot grant anticipatory bail relief when the application itself is premature. The ruling addresses the limits of judicial intervention in anticipatory-bail proceedings and the requirement that the statutory stage for such relief must arise.

title: Supreme Court considers seven-judge bench hearing on additional State levy over sales tax
summary: The Supreme Court has listed a seven-judge Bench hearing for September 22 concerning the constitutional question of whether States can impose an additional levy over sales tax. The matter raises important questions concerning legislative and fiscal powers.

title: Supreme Court agrees to hear plea against disruption of essential services during protests
summary: The Supreme Court has agreed to consider a plea concerning disruption of services during protests. The proceedings involve questions concerning public order, citizens' rights and the legal limits applicable to protest-related disruption.

title: Lok Sabha refers FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 to Joint Parliamentary Committee
summary: The Lok Sabha has referred the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act Amendment Bill, 2026 to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for further examination. The legislative process will now involve detailed scrutiny of the proposed amendments.

title: Supreme Court directs CBI probe into custodial death case
summary: The Supreme Court has ordered a CBI investigation into the custodial death of a person who died several days after being taken into custody in 2024. The case raises questions concerning custodial safeguards, investigation and accountability of law-enforcement authorities.

title: Supreme Court considers balanced demolition policy protecting shelter rights
summary: The Supreme Court has allowed an NGO to approach governments with a representation seeking a balanced policy concerning demolition of unauthorised structures while protecting shelter rights. The development involves the balance between regulatory enforcement and constitutional concerns relating to housing and dignity.
